title: How Far the Price of a Keyturn Vehicle Listing May Move in a Day
content:
The most a price may move in a day is settled from how long the listing has been live and what its fault record shows rather than from the class, and no lockout period runs against the listing after a price is changed.

1. A Keyturn Vehicle Listing that has been live for 365 calendar days or more with no fault report in the rolling twelve months counted back from the handling date moves at 0.25 of the price asked in a day, twenty-five hundredths.

2. A listing live for 365 calendar days or more with at least one fault report in that window moves at 0.2 of the price asked, twenty hundredths.

3. Any other listing moves at the standard movement rate.

### Reading the two conditions

| Listing live for | Fault reports in the rolling twelve months | Movement in a day |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 365 calendar days or more | none | 0.25 of the price asked |
| 365 calendar days or more | 1 or more | 0.2 of the price asked |
| fewer than 365 calendar days | any | the standard movement rate |

A listing live for exactly 365 calendar days is on one of the first two rows, the test being met at the figure; one live for 364 calendar days is on the third row whatever its fault record shows. A listing live for three years with a single fault report dated inside the window moves at 0.2, and the same listing once that report falls outside the rolling twelve months moves at 0.25.

*Worked on a hypothetical price.* A price asked of 200.00 USD moving at 0.25 may fall no further than 150.00 USD in the day; the same price moving at 0.2 may fall no further than 160.00 USD.
